lesson_title: Correction and reflection: advanced composition, production, and literacy
task_label: Music theory and listening — Correction and reflection
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Music — Creating
essential_question: How do extended techniques and larger forms sustain a longer musical idea?
learning_objectives: Use error evidence to correct work on advanced composition, production, and literacy and demonstrate corrected understanding on a fresh item.
Communicate understanding of advanced composition, production, and literacy using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on advanced composition, production, and literacy against the stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on advanced composition, production, and literacy.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: manuscript paper or accessible notation tool
instrument, voice, or keyboard — a silent or written route is always available

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 12 of "Advanced Composition, Production, and Literacy" (unit 2, grade 11) is a correction and reflection on advanced composition, production, and literacy. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Compose or produce an extended original work with score or session documentation and analytical commentary. Today's work contributes to that by handling advanced composition, production, and literacy at the correction and reflection stage, against the unit's wider topics of extended harmonic and modal materials, counterpoint and texture, advanced form and development, and production and engineering choices. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Revise your earlier work on advanced composition, production, and literacy and document the revision rather than quietly replacing it. Build a revision log: what specifically was not working, what you now believe caused it, the change you made, and how you can tell the change helped. Keep the before and after side by side. Then write what pattern connects the problems you found — a habit of rushing one stage, a technique not yet secure, an intent never stated clearly — and one thing you will do differently that would catch it sooner. Honest documentation of a weak result scores fully here. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about advanced composition, production, and literacy, and it belongs to "Advanced Composition, Production, and Literacy", which also covers separate topics such as extended harmonic and modal materials. Close out with this check before you stop: For one corrected item, state the original error, its cause, and the check that would catch it next time. At grade 11 the bar is independent work with sustained self-direction: you set the constraint, defend it, and revise on the evidence of your own checks rather than on being told to.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task on advanced composition, production, and literacy., The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Use error evidence to correct work on advanced composition, production, and literacy and demonstrate corrected understanding on a fresh item.
Produce the deliverable for a correction and reflection: Revision log with cause/change/evidence per problem, before-and-after versions kept, a named pattern, and one practice change.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: Revision log with cause/change/evidence per problem, before-and-after versions kept, a named pattern, and one practice change.
critique_criteria: The revision log records what was not working, the diagnosed cause, the change made, and how improvement can be told.
Before and after versions are both kept and comparable.
A pattern connecting the problems is named rather than each treated in isolation.
One concrete change of practice is stated.
Honest documentation of a weak result is scored on the documentation, not on the strength of the original piece.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task centres a visual element (advanced composition, production, and literacy). Provide tactile, raised-line, or high-relief equivalents, enlarged and high-contrast print, and a verbal description route. Never make colour discrimination alone carry a criterion — pair any colour judgement with value, label, or texture.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting advanced composition, production, and literacy.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for advanced composition, production, and literacy follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for advanced composition, production, and literacy, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to advanced composition, production, and literacy works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of advanced composition, production, and literacy, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking advanced composition, production, and literacy mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply advanced composition, production, and literacy under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on advanced composition, production, and literacy rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
